what: End-to-end runs of the decoders C5 prices, and a config-level comparison of two Qwen generations
why: C5 reads published configs and computes decode state. Arithmetic over a config is a hypothesis about a model; loading the weights is the test. These runs check what actually fits, what it costs, and -- in the Qwen case -- whether reading configs can see a generation change at all.

patches_needed: TextModel loads the decoder from `model.*`, but a multimodal checkpoint keeps it at `model.language_model.*`, so text-only loading of gemma-4-E2B-it fails at model.embed_tokens.weight. Added a constructor taking the decoder's own prefix.
the example hardcodes bf16 on GPU, which needs sm_80; added a --dtype flag so an sm_75 card can ask for f16.
runs.patch_is_behaviour_preserving: the prefix change only alters where the decoder loads from: the constructor's other uses of the unprefixed builder are dtype() and device(), which are prefix-independent, and the one root-level weight (lm_head) is not reached because this config sets tie_word_embeddings=true
runs.conclusion: the fork's gemma4 generates through this path but its f16 output is wrong, and its default bf16 cannot run on sm_75 at all -- so gemma-4 could not be validated through the fork on a T4

qwen_generation_comparison.claim: Qwen3.6-27B and Qwen3.8-27B are the same architecture
qwen_generation_comparison.method: both config.json files flattened and compared key by key
qwen_generation_comparison.the_difference: transformers_version: 4.57.1 against 5.8.0.dev0 -- the library that wrote the file
qwen_generation_comparison.shared: 64 layers, hidden 5120, 24 query heads over 4 KV heads, head_dim 256, intermediate 17408, vocab 248320, 48 linear-attention layers interleaved with 16 full-attention ones at interval 4, one MTP layer
qwen_generation_comparison.conclusion: identical parameter counts and identical shapes. Whatever separates these generations at 27B is weights, data or post-training, and no amount of reading configs will find it -- which is the limit of C5's method, measured.
qwen_generation_comparison.caveat: the two GGUF files differ in size (12.0 GB against 10.9 GB) at the same nominal 3.0625 bpw, so the quantiser allocated bits differently between them. The throughput figures above are therefore not perfectly matched, and the 0.7 tok/s gap should not be read as a model difference.

not_run.Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next: 360 GB of weights; out of reach on any accelerator available here
not_run.bf16 or AWQ Qwen 27B: 55.6 GB bf16, and 20.4/21.0 GB as 4-bit AWQ, against a 15.4 GB T4 -- the GGUF route at 3 bpw is what made these runnable at all
not_run.deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite via candle: the fork's deepseekv2 example exposes no quantization flag, so it loads 31.4 GB of f16 weights -- twice what a T4 holds. The library has quantized loading (TextModel::new_with_quant takes a GgmlDType), but the example does not wire it up.
not_run.Qwen3.6 / Qwen3.8 via candle: candle-transformers has qwen3_5.rs, but the fork ships no example binary for it, so there is nothing to run without writing one
